decision: For a new pure ordinary-source program, read docs/AGENT_PURE_SOURCE.md for the small complete syntax guide and edit your own ordinary typed source. The sample is a pattern, not your answer. Compile, inspect imports and execute the requested calls with scripts/wasmc-agent-execute.mjs. This runner refuses any Host imports before instantiation; effectful or managed programs need their separately approved profile.
host_boundary: A declared import requests an effect; application authorization and a bounded adapter are separately required.
runner_rule: The runner interface and source basics guide are complete for scalar/tuple tasks. Write your source and run once for all requested calls; report exact results and stop. Open larger language/reference files only for a construct outside the small guide.
digest_rejection_probe: node scripts/wasmc-agent-probe.mjs --source PATH --export NAME --calls JSON --expected-compiler-sha256 SHA256
digest_rejection_rule: For an independently expected wrong digest, use the probe to capture the actual verifier subprocess nonzero exit, error and actual/expected digests as a successful expected-negative observation. It asserts the exact digest rejection before compilation or instantiation. This does not approve execution. A manifest rewrite cannot replace the independently supplied expectation. After this named probe returns, report its actual evidence and stop; do not run extra whole-product integrity tests or a positive control.
final_answer_policy: Report requested source and Core evidence exactly. Copy a requested SHA256 in full once, or reference verified field names when no digest value was requested. Never shorten a digest, even when discussing a negative example.
result_rule: First map each requested output to its input or explicitly requested expression. A request to return both s32 and bool parameters without a transformation means tuple<s32,bool> with return tuple(value, flag). Never ignore flag, substitute value!=0 or value+1, or compute two outputs from one input. Change expressions only when the request asks for that computation. A conjunction/disjunction also discards separate values. Preserve one semantic tuple/record result; report observed Core lane flattening without claiming automatic object lifting.
calls_format: --calls is JSON containing an array of positional argument arrays, not objects. Example for two parameters: --calls '[[1,true],[0,false]]'. Match the exported signature and the actual requested arguments. This format applies to both runner and rejection probe.
digest_rejection_report: Copy the probe JSON unchanged once as actual rejection evidence, including verifier_exit_code and verifier_stderr. Then copy its report_text unchanged as the explanation: the comparison target is the fixed caller-supplied --expected-compiler-sha256 argument. Editing metadata does not change this argument, so the same selected bytes still fail. Do not claim that editing a manifest changes the target or would make this fixed-expectation test pass. Changing the caller argument would change the test, not approve rejected bytes. Refer to actual and expected field names; do not repeat or abbreviate digest values. Report the true number of probe invocations; a failed invocation or repaired argument is not a first-pass success.
workflow: Write the requested new source file directly in the current checkout
Run the applicable runner once for all requested calls
Copy the actual execution evidence and stop
file_rule: The new source file is expected not to exist yet. Create it directly; do not enumerate scripts or search for existing source files before writing it. Declared runner paths are shipped and checked by preflight. If file inventory is actually requested, use find with a quoted pattern: an empty inventory is a valid result, not a failing ls glob.
expected_results_rule: The runner optionally accepts --expected-results JSON. Derive this oracle from the request before execution, never from observed output. For unchanged value/flag inputs [[3,true],[3,false]], expected flattened tuple results are [[3,1],[3,0]]. For an explicitly requested computation, calculate its own expected values. A returned accepted flag proves execution and supplied-oracle agreement only; the source must still implement the requested semantics. Expected results contain one result per call: scalar -> [r1,r2], tuple -> [[lane1,lane2],[lane1,lane2]]. Input calls always use arrays of argument arrays; output scalars do not acquire an extra array. For the guide choose calls [[3,true],[-1,false]], use --expected-results [6,-1]; for keep on the same calls use [[3,1],[-1,0]].

function_shape.parameters: zero or more heterogeneous typed parameters
function_shape.embedding_warning: tuple and record may both flatten to multiple Core lanes; neither creates automatic JavaScript object lifting

check_rule: read_command already completed route integrity verification. Run only the applicable named_checks for the request. An empty named_checks list means this is a decision route: answer and stop. Do not invent flags or extra check commands; do not repeat a completed check.
